payload.goal: Make phase status writable at the same tier as task status. 32 of 125 completed phases across 15 initiatives still render active or pending, because phase_status_changed has no first-class tool — only sofar_update_plan's full replace or the MCP-less event append dialect. Consequence: 'Active phase' names finished work in 14 of the 16 records that render the line, and the digest's Current/Next task lines vanish because status.ts scopes them to the active phase. Settled up front on measurement: MCP-only, no CLI sibling.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Settle the write path (blocks everything else)

tasks.title: Confirm ZERO new event types. phase_status_changed and task_added already exist, fold correctly (fold.ts:997 and fold.ts:1003) and are rendered everywhere. Verify their payload shapes in packages/schema/src are sufficient for a granular tool, so this initiative adds tool surface only — the record-graph guarantee. Refute before building.

DECIDE the phase-status mechanism. (a) sofar_update_phase mirroring sofar_update_task; (b) extend update_task to implicitly close its parent phase; (c) DERIVE phase status in the fold when every task resolves. (c) is the trap: it eliminates the defect and destroys doctor's stale-phase axis, which exists precisely to express 'tasks done, phase not finished'. Log the decision.

Log the MCP-only ruling as a decision, citing the measurement: CLI event append 61.5ms (50.5ms of it spawn plus full-bundle parse) against ~11ms for an MCP call on the already-running server, plus a second process because the PostToolUse matcher Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash catches the Bash call and never matches mcp__sofar__*, plus event append resolving by branch alone with no session pin (record-integrity M1). Benchmark: scratchpad/bench-paths.sh.
Schema: UpdatePhaseArgs {initiative?, phase, status, note?} and its JSON schema entry, in packages/schema/src ONLY — the guard-rail holds, no schema anywhere else.
mcp/update-phase.ts mirroring update-task.ts (34 lines): resolveWriteInitiative pin so a peer's branch switch cannot misroute it, one appendAndProject, typed result.

Idempotence and error shape: already at this status appends nothing (the close-initiative precedent); an unknown phase name returns a typed error and never a silent no-op, since phases are addressed by free-text name and a typo would otherwise vanish.
Register in mcp/server.ts and confirm the tool table renders; the MCP-less dialect keeps reaching the same event through event append, so no caller is stranded.

DECIDE whether add_task is in scope. task_added has NO emitter anywhere in packages/engine/src — only the two consumers, fold.ts:1003 and index-reach.ts:248 — and 3 uses across the entire 36-initiative record. Confirm it is dead rather than merely rare before building, or rule it out of scope and say why.
If in scope: mcp/add-task.ts plus schema, mirroring 2.x. Must not disturb plan_updated's full-replace contract, on which SPEC's forward-compatibility story rests (task-drop-state D2).

DECIDE repair versus leave-as-history. doctor --fix never touches record prose (SPEC §CLI), so this is a ruling, not a build. If repair: a one-off operator action, never a shipped command, and it must append real phase_status_changed events rather than rewriting history.
docs/SPEC.md is authoritative: the new tool(s) in §MCP tools and their §Acceptance criteria. No task is done until its criteria pass.
Tests: one event per call, idempotent re-issue appends nothing, session pin survives a parallel branch rebind, unknown phase errors typed, and replay stays deterministic.
Dogfood: close THIS initiative's own phases with the new tool as each completes, then re-run doctor and confirm the stale-phase count falls from 32. The dogfood IS the acceptance evidence.

payload.because: Measured this session on the installed binary (N=15, mean): `sofar event append` costs 61.5ms, of which 50.5ms is process spawn plus full-bundle parse and only ~11ms is the actual record work; an MCP call on the already-running server costs that ~11ms alone. The CLI path also spawns a SECOND process, because the PostToolUse matcher is Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash and never matches mcp__sofar__*, so every Bash-issued sofar command fires a hook that reads the command, applies the record-hygiene D1 self-recording exemption and appends nothing. End to end that is ~92ms across 2 processes against ~11ms across 0 — roughly 8x. Correctness decides it independently of speed: `sofar event append` resolves by branch alone and never consults the session home (record-integrity M1, and AppendArgs.slug documents it), so on this shared worktree, where peers rebind branches mid-session, the CLI path can misroute the write that this initiative exists to make reliable. Precedent agrees — task status has no CLI writer either. The existing dual-path commands are dual because they touch bindings.json or the git branch, which an MCP call cannot sensibly do; phase status touches nothing outside the log. Benchmark: scratchpad/bench-paths.sh.
payload.chose: Phase status gets an MCP tool ONLY — no `sofar phase` CLI sibling. The MCP-less convention dialect keeps reaching phase_status_changed through `sofar event append`, exactly as it already reaches task_status_changed, so no caller is stranded.
payload.over: (a) A CLI command alongside the MCP tool, mirroring `close` and `remember` which are both dual-path. (b) CLI-only, keeping every plan-structure write in the convention dialect.
payload.rule: Phase and task-structure writes are MCP-only — never add a CLI writer for them; the convention dialect uses `sofar event append`.

payload.note: Settled as D1 with the benchmark inline: CLI 61.5ms (50.5ms of it spawn + full-bundle parse) and a second hook process, against ~11ms MCP on the running server; plus event append's branch-only resolution (record-integrity M1). Benchmark at scratchpad/bench-paths.sh.

payload.next_action: Task 1.1: confirm phase_status_changed and task_added need no schema change, then rule 1.2 on the mechanism. Awaiting user go-ahead separately on where the doctor liveness-grading defect lives, and on adding the fast-bundle size budget to speed-2 as a new task.
payload.summary: Opened phase-lifecycle: 5 phases, 13 tasks. Created without binding, so main stays on drift-certification and peers are unaffected; this session was re-homed via start_session rather than writing in with explicit initiative args, which is the leak shape diagnosed live in peer sofar-1b. D1 settles the MCP-only placement on measurement and is a standing constraint. Task 1.3 done. Open and genuinely undecided: 1.2 the mechanism, where deriving phase status in the fold is the trap because it destroys doctor's stale-phase axis; and 3.1 whether add_task is in scope. Separately found and NOT yet homed: doctor grades a torn or leaked session by whether a session_ended exists, so any session in the parallel-wrap window is reported as settled history with the write pin preventing new splits, while it is still adding events to the unregistered record. Live instance: session ecd42534 in commit-attribution, 28 events, graded WARN.
